summary: Your LDL ('bad') cholesterol is higher than recommended, while your HDL ('good') cholesterol and triglycerides look fine. High LDL raises long-term heart risk, so it's worth a conversation with your doctor.

tests.name: Total cholesterol
tests.explanation: The total amount of cholesterol in your blood is above the desirable level.

tests.name: LDL cholesterol
tests.explanation: LDL can build up in artery walls; yours is above the recommended level.

tests.name: HDL cholesterol
tests.explanation: HDL helps clear cholesterol; yours is in the healthy range.

tests.name: Triglycerides
tests.explanation: Triglycerides are a type of blood fat; yours are normal.

keyFindings: LDL cholesterol is high at 162 mg/dL (recommended below 100).
Total cholesterol is high at 228 mg/dL.
HDL and triglycerides are within healthy limits.

generalTips: Regular brisk walking most days of the week supports healthy cholesterol.
